question: Does higher crop-rotation diversity (CDL 5-yr window ending t-1) reduce drought loss cost (RMA drought indemnity / liability) for insured corn in county x year data, 2013-2024?
hazard: NASA POWER hazard_z (JJA composite of -SPI, EDD>30C, -root-zone wetness; z vs 1991-2020); high-hazard = hazard_z > 1, low-hazard placebo = hazard_z < 0
outcome: corn lcr_drought (drought indemnity / liability), weighted by liability in acre-equivalents; principal crops as secondary

bowles_2020.citation: Bowles TM et al. (2020) Long-term evidence shows that crop-rotation diversification increases agricultural resilience to adverse growing conditions in North America. One Earth 2(3):284-293. doi:10.1016/j.oneear.2020.02.007
bowles_2020.finding: diversified rotations reduced maize yield losses in drought years by 14-90% across 11 long-term North American trials (relative to simple rotations)

share_3plus.unit: share of cropland pixels with >= 3 crop classes in the 5-yr window
share_3plus.per_label: +10 percentage points of cropland in 3+ crop rotations

n_crops_5y.unit: mean distinct crop classes per pixel in the 5-yr window

bowles_comparison.contrasts: share_3plus: all remaining 2-crop cropland moved to 3+ crop rotations; n_crops_5y: +1 crop class per pixel; div_shannon_5y: +0.66 (corn-soy -> 4-crop window)
bowles_comparison.note: Positive = diversity reduces drought loss cost. Trials measure field yield-loss reduction; RMA loss cost is indemnity below a guarantee, aggregated over a county, so magnitudes are not directly comparable. Extrapolating a county slope to a 100% switch is far outside the observed within-county range.

app_effect.form: fields moved from simple to 3+ crop rotations lose r less in drought years: county drought loss multiplier m(s) = (1 - r*s) / (1 - r*s_now), s = share of cropland in 3+ crop rotations
app_effect.label: Scenario assumption, not an estimate from the county data: field trials (Bowles et al. 2020) found 14-90% smaller maize drought-year yield losses in diversified rotations. est = trial lower bound (14%); lo = no effect (the county data show no robust effect); hi = trial upper bound (90%).

verdict: Data: 7463 insured-corn county-years (2013-2024, 631 counties), 630 high-hazard (NASA POWER hazard_z > 1), mostly 2021-2023; 2012 cannot be used with a lagged 5-year CDL window (CDL starts 2008). Primary treatment share_3plus (share of cropland in 3+ crop rotations, window ending t-1): only 11% of its variance is within county (within SD 0.053 vs between 0.153). Across counties it tracks crop mix and geography (Spearman with corn share -0.70, irrigation +0.20, longitude -0.32, mean corn drought loss cost +0.51). Effect on corn drought loss cost in high-hazard years per +10 percentage points of cropland in 3+ crop rotations: county FE + state-year FE OLS +12.6% (95% CI +4.6 to +20.5); PPML +4.4% (95% CI -9.7 to +20.7); pooled with controls +11.6% (95% CI +5.2 to +18.1). Negative = protective. Secondary treatments (FE OLS): n_crops_5y per +0.1 crops +0.2% (95% CI -4.3 to +4.7); Shannon per +0.1 -14.5% (95% CI -24.4 to -4.7), but Shannon PPML -1.6% (95% CI -17.9 to +17.9). Diagnostics (primary): low-hazard placebo passes; excess-moisture placebo FAILS; lead test passes; robust to a confounder as strong as hazard x irrigation: yes (robustness value 0.041). Shannon: lead test FAILS, excess-moisture placebo FAILS, robust to irrigation-strength confounder: no. Adding 2012 via the contemporaneous Shannon window (includes the crop planted in year t, before the summer hazard): +32.2% (95% CI +20.9 to +43.4) per +0.1 Shannon. Verdict: NO robust observational effect. The primary 'how many crops' measure is wrong-signed (more 3+ crop rotation, more corn drought loss) within counties. The Shannon index does look protective in the linear FE model, but it does not survive the proportional (PPML) model, the lead test, the excess-moisture placebo or a confounder as strong as irrigation. It also flips to a harmful sign when 2012 is added through the contemporaneous window. County-year insurance data with little within-county change in rotations cannot confirm (or rule out) the field-trial effect. The app therefore shows the Bowles et al. (2020) trial range (14-90% smaller drought-year maize yield losses) as a labelled scenario assumption, with the low end (no effect) included in its range.
